rules.title: New Jersey Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about criminal history on applications or orally/in writing before making a conditional offer. They may never consider non-conviction, expunged, sealed, pardoned, vacated or juvenile records. After an offer they may consider only listed serious convictions within set look-back periods. Any withdrawal needs written reasons and an individualized assessment.
rules.key_value: No criminal-history inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 yrs (1st degree), 4 yrs (2nd/3rd), 1 yr (4th)
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.effective_date_note: Computed: approved June 18, 2021; effective first day of the seventh month next following enactment = January 1, 2022.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 (first violation), $5,000 (second within 5 years), $10,000 (two or more others within 7 years); enforced via Division on Civil Rights complaint, not court action; director may order return of application fee and up to $1,000 to applicant.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing providers offering rental dwelling units.

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

parsed.doc_summary: Text of New Jersey P.L. 2021, c.110, the Fair Chance in Housing Act (N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 et seq.), which limits criminal-history screening of rental applicants. Effective 2022-01-01 by computation from the June 18, 2021 approval date.
